Pity the poor researcher who works only with a homogenous population. My laboratory welcomes all. Before my blade, all are equal!|From the private journal of Doctor [[Demagol]].|<ref name="SJDD" />}}
During the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the Mandalorian [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Demagol]] used the conquered people of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] as subjects for his grisly studies. He was particularly interested in finding a biological base for Jedi powers. Initially, Jedi were kidnapped for this purpose, before hostilities with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] surfaced,<ref name="KOTORH">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Handbook]]''</ref> and a number of Jedi captured on [[Suurja]] poured into his lab on [[Flashpoint Stellar Research Station|Flashpoint Station]], to serve as new research subjects.<ref name="KOTOR8">[[Knights of the Old Republic 8|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 8]]</ref> Demagol's methods of research included the rack, irradiation, electroshock and vivisection. Some of his test subjects died.<ref name="SJDD" />

When the [[Arkanian Offshoot/Legends|Arkanian Offshoot]] [[Jarael]] was captured by Mandalorians while impersonating a Jedi, she was taken to Flashpoint, where other Jedi were being tortured and tested by Demagol. After arriving she met with [[Darth Malak|Squint]], a Jedi who had also been made into a prisoner. Upon seeing that he had a new test subject, Demagol wanted to study Jarael immediately. Squint, however, protested and insisted that he go in Jarael's place since he had already discerned that she was not a Jedi, and knew that there were trials only a Jedi could survive.<ref name="KOTOR8" />

Roughly ten years before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] was captured and brought before the famed scientist [[Jenna Zan Arbor]], who was studying the traits of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] individuals (with hopes of genetically engineering Force sensitivity into normal beings). Her "experiments" included phlebotomy and torture, designed to test Qui-Gon's endurance.<ref name="Experiment" />

The scientist [[Leonis Murthé]] was fond of experimenting on living beings, finding new ways to make them die and experimenting with how long he could keep them screaming. Active during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and years afterwards, the doctor eventually admitted that he gave up any science pretense long ago, and was simply doing it for his own personal pleasure.<ref name="BFAD" />

Dr. [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]], also known as "Doctor Death," was a notorious [[Gender/Legends|man]] posing as a medical [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] in order to use his patients as subjects for unauthorized and often fatal experiments. Evazan had the [[Death/Legends|death]] sentence in twelve [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], and was wanted for murder, medical malpractice, practicing medicine without a license, assault, and torture.<ref name="City" />

==Secret locations==
===''Anakin Solo''===
During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], [[Darth Caedus]] had the [[Embrace of Pain]] installed in a secret hangar bay on board his command ship, the [[Anakin Solo (starship)|''Anakin Solo'']]. There, he used the Embrace to torture his cousin, [[Ben Skywalker]], hoping to turn him to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark side of the Force]].<ref name="I" />

===''Lusankya''===
In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], when the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class]] [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' was commissioned for use by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], it was taken to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and buried underneath Imperial City. While stationed there, a section of the ''Lusankya'' was used as a private corrections facility by the [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]], [[Ysanne Isard]]. To thwart any potential escape attempts, the prison was fitted with a rotating artificial gravity generator. Prisoners believed they were right-side up, but in truth, were upside down, so that any attempts to dig themselves to freedom would only lead them deeper within the prison.

[[File:Lusankya-CE5.png|thumb|left|250px|The [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class]] [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'']]
Isard used the dreadnought's facilities for her Imperial intelligence-gathering needs, usually including torture and interrogation.<ref name="NEC" /> Captives were tortured to collect secrets, and selected prisoners were turned into sleeper agents.<ref name="GOI" /> Isard was ruthless during interrogation sessions, employing multiple methods as required&mdash;torture, drugs, and psychological conditioning&mdash;to learn what she desired.<ref name="NEC" />

[[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] native [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]] was also sent to the ''Lusankya'', having been captured during a failed spy mission to Coruscant. Isard tried to condition Celchu and turn him into one of her agents, but the methods were too extreme and left him catatonic.<ref name="WG">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref> The [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] was imprisoned within the bowels of the ''Lusankya'', where he was tortured by Isard for vital [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] secrets. When Isard realized that Horn would reveal nothing, she had him placed in the general population of the prison, from which he would later escape.<ref name="XWKT" />

===Secret bunkers===
During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], several secret interrogation chambers existed close to the solid surface of [[Galactic City/Legends|Imperial City]]. The constructions were disguised as nondescript, run-down buildings, but in reality, they were sealed bunkers protected by strong metal walls. The inside of the bunkers were a showcase of tools designed to induce pain: racks, bed platforms with manacles and electrical rods, pain-inducing drugs and serums, interrogation droids, and so on.<ref name="JASB" />

After the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]] capture of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[EVS-6962]], a [[EVS Construction Droid|construction droid]] under the supervision of [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], inadvertently uncovered a secret Imperial Interrogation Center during its routine tear-down assignments.<ref name="EGD" />

==Consequences==
{{Quote|Okay, Dad, I was interrogating her and she died. Do you really want to know the details?''"<br />"''It kind of makes a difference, Jacen.''"<br />"''I used a mind-invasion technique to make her talk. She must have had some physical weakness. She died of an aneurysm.|Jacen Solo, describing to Han Solo, the death of Ailyn Vel during interrogation.|<ref name="Bloodlines" />}}
[[File:ChamberofPersuasion.jpg|thumb|right|220px|A captive [[Marasiah Fel]], wounded and physically and mentally exhausted after suffering torture at the hands of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]]]
The mere threat of torture was often enough to cause the most determined resistors to cooperate. [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protector]] [[Mirta Gev]] was one such individual. While under the custody of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Caedus]] and his apprentice [[Tahiri Veila]], Gev was threatened with disfigurement; [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] Veila intended on misshaping Gev's face, if she refused to disclose who it was that cut off Lord Caedus's arm. Mortified by the threat, Gev relented, and told everything she knew.<ref name="Invincible" />

Threats of torture could also force an individual to torture others. [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Akanseh]] was an accomplished surgeon and a great philanthropist who was captured by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Moff Sarne confiscated Akanseh's private medical suite, and forced the doctor to work for him as an interrogator. Akanseh tried to carry out his duties in his own manner. Rather than resorting to torture, he attempted to convince his subjects to trust him enough to disclose the information willingly. He knew that if he couldn't obtain the information in this manner, the prisoner would be turned over to Imperial interrogators and their savage [[Droid/Legends|droids]], or worse, Akanseh might be forced to perform the act himself. Once, while interrogating a stubborn resistance fighter, Sarne decided to drop in for a spot inspection to make sure the doctor was performing accordingly. Akanseh was forced to chemically torture the prisoner, or face the same fate himself if he didn't produce results soon. After being freed by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] forces, Akanseh joined the crew of the [[FarStar]] corvette, who were tasked to hunt down Moff Sarne. Deeply regretful of his service as Sarne's interrogators, he hoped to make up for what had done.<ref name="DC" />

===Temporary effects===
The pain inflicted on the victim during the actual torture section would often linger for a long time, days or hours, after the ordeal was over. The victim might feel that it hurt to breathe, to wear clothes, to swallow.<ref name="GS" /> Other temporary effects included dizziness,<ref name="CTE" /> fatigue,<ref name="SWEV" /> extreme physical or mental exhaustion,<ref name="CTE" /> numbness, shivering, a raw or hoarse voice (due to the victim's screams), slurring, confusion, a nasal quality to the voice (due to a broken nose), temporary loss of memory (for example, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Dirk Harkness]] had difficulties remembering his own name after being tortured by [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]]),<ref name="GS" /> catatonia<ref name="KR">''[[The Kathol Rift]]''</ref> and blackout.<ref name="DT8" />

===Physical injuries===
[[File:Dama-torture.jpg|thumb|left|215px|Common facial damages of torture, shown in [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Dama Montalvo]], after an interrogation session with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]]]
Burns,<ref name="Ascension" /><ref name="SOTME" /> cuts,<ref name="R60" /> puncture wounds, gouges<ref name="Ascension" /> and bruises<ref name="Bloodlines" /> were common effects of torture. Eyes glued shut, a black eye or two, split lips, swollen eyes, a broken nose and swollen lips were common facial injuries.<ref name="P" /> More serious effects included disfigurement,<ref name="Invincible" /> broken bones,<ref name="R13" /> broken teeth,<ref name="Bloodlines" /> calcification of the skeleton,<ref name="The Truce at Bakura">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> an elongated spine (from the rack),<ref name="SJDD" /> permanent brain damage,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">[[Neuronic whip/Legends|Neuronic whip]] in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> loss of limbs, and loss of one or more appendages and outer organs, like eyes or ears.<ref name="Invincible" />

===Mental damage===
{{Quote|Look at&hellip; what is left of him. Do you think saving his life would be a kindness?|LE-914 ("Ellie") after Tay Vanis, a victim of Imperial torture, is found by his fellow Rebels|<ref name="LE" />}}
Wounds and burns could be cleaned up with sufficient [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] treatment, and body parts could be replaced by [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]].<ref name="NEGWT" /> Mental damage would take considerably more.<ref name="KR" /> Torture could seriously harm the victim mentally. If they were lucky, they would only relive the ordeal in their nightmares;<ref name="F" /> many individuals were badly traumatized, sometimes to the point of being unable to speak. This was the case with many of the citizens who were introduced to the [[IT-O interrogation droid/Legends|IT-O Interrogator]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] after being unlucky enough to be rounded up by the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="IT-O NEGD" /> Some torture victims succumbed to madness<ref>''[[The New Jedi Order: Traitor]]'' and ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Ties That Bind]]''</ref> or were brainwashed.<ref name="MBME" /> During an experiment by the Imperial commander [[Rezi Soresh]] to create the perfect [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]], the "winner," [[X-7]], was tortured and brainwashed to the point of not remembering his real name or his past, and didn't recognize the person staring back at him when he looked in the mirror.<ref name="Rebel Force: Target">''[[Rebel Force: Target]]''</ref> During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], it was rumored that the [[Emperor's Shadow Guard]], mute, ruthless [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-wielding warriors, were [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] captured and tortured by Darth Sidious, their minds so broken that they could not even speak.<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed comic">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|''The Force Unleashed'' comic]]</ref>

Some victims were tortured into insanity.<ref name="L49" /> Other were so broken mentally that they simply existed as mindless shells.<ref name="LE">[[Star Wars (1977) 80|''Star Wars'' (1977) 80]] and [[LE manifest droid]] in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> Victims of torture could also suffer from mental suffering like catatonia, paranoia and egomania.<ref name="KR" /> About a millennium before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], the [[Gen'Dai/Legends|Gen'Dai]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Durge/Legends|Durge]] became a victim of unspeakable torture at the hands of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], who turned his species' natural longevity against him, finding ways of inflicting pain throughout his scattered nerves. Unable to die, his already dangerous psyche was pushed further past the brink of sanity.<ref name="DBD">{{DB|character|durge|Durge}}</ref>

Curiously, some torture victims would come to respect and admire their tormentors. [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] bonded with [[Vergere]] this way, after she tortured him for [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]]. Vergere was old and experienced, and serving her own agenda, and had been able to manipulate Jacen's growing psyche. This was a case of a psychological phenomenon in which hostages would grow strangely attached to their captors. Sometimes, captives even grew to love their warders, particularly if the warder was skilled enough in manipulating people.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''. This phenomenon is known as the [[Wikipedia:Stockholm syndrome|Stockholm syndrome]].</ref>

Prior to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] hero [[Tay Vanis]] was captured and tortured by Darth Vader, who left him a mindless shell of a man. After Vanis was found by his fellow Rebels, his droid [[LE-914]] ("Ellie") destroyed both herself and her master, as an act of mercy killing.<ref name="LE" />

Mental post-torture traumas could be treated, at least to a certain degree, by placing the victim in hypno-trance and administering anti-trauma deprogramming.<ref name="DM">{{JournalCite|10|Desperate Measures}}</ref>

[[File:TayVanis.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tay Vanis, reduced to a mindless shell after being tortured by Darth Vader]]
Sometimes, torture would be the catalyst in a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-user's]] descent to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. This was the case of [[Kam Solusar]], who was tortured by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Sedriss QL]] until he submitted.<ref name="NEGC" /> After the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Halagad Ventor]] was captured by the Empire, and tortured by Darth Vader himself. As Vader broke down Ventor's mental shields, Ventor told him everything he wanted to know, and was consumed by the dark side.<ref name="Domain of Evil">''[[Domain of Evil]]''</ref>

Sith were known for torturing Jedi with physical agony to try and corrupt captive Jedi to the dark side.<ref name="Old" /> During the quest to find the ancient [[Star Forge]], Jedi Knight Bastila Shan and soldier [[Carth Onasi]] were captured by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Saul Karath]] and tortured into revealing Jedi secrets. Later, when Bastila was freed, she was then confronted by Darth Malak, and tortured with needles<ref name="Shadows and Light">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref> and relentless barrages of Sith lightning.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Malak tortured Bastila for days,<ref name="Old" /> until she, unable to withstand the assault any longer, gave into the dark side, and became the Dark Lord's new apprentice.<ref name="KOTOR" />

In year [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], the Jedi apprentice [[Lowbacca]], along with his fellow apprentices Jacen and Jaina Solo, was kidnapped and taken to the [[Shadow Academy]]. There, he was locked in a room where he was repeatedly exposed to high-pitched, ear-piercing sound, flashing, blinding lights, and jets of near-freezing water at extremely high pressure. The only way to stop his suffering would be to smash the sonic generator, which was incredibly heavy and reinforced, so the only way to destroy it would be to call upon the dark side of the Force. Eventually, Lowbacca could no longer endure, and smashed the generator in a fit of rage and horror.<ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref>

===Suicide===
{{Quote|The military has to do this nobody-gets-left-behind thing because it's part of holding a team together. But us, sweetheart - we work ''alone''. And one day, maybe we'll need to leave ''you'' behind. Be sure you can handle that. There's a special capsule for you, because when we say no prisoners, we mean it.|[[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] recruiter, explaining the realities of an agent's life to Hallena Devis|<ref name="NP" />}}
Often, if the opportunity arose, the victim would gladly kill themselves rather than getting tortured. One incident was the [[Cerean/Legends|Cerean]] [[Con artist/Legends|grifter]] [[Toh Revo Chryyx]], who somehow managed to stop his own heart before he could be delivered to the feared [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Rokko]] the Hutt.<ref name="JT" /> Majordomo [[Ob Fortuna]] strangled himself to death with a length of cable rather than facing his former employers in the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters Guild]].<ref name="SS">''[[Slave Ship]]''</ref>

During the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] agents were issued tiny pellets containing a fast-acting [[Poison/Legends|poison]]. The tablets were insurance in case she or he was captured with no hope of escape, as a quick way out before the agent could compromise the Republic; Intelligence agent [[Hallena Devis]] kept hers in a [[Snuff box|snuff container]] in a wallet in her pants.<ref name="NP">''[[The Clone Wars: No Prisoners]]''</ref>

Suicide was also a standard trick for members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="RB">{{GamerCite|6|Rebel Bass}}</ref> When the Rebel [[Bria Tharen]] and her [[Red Hand Squadron]] were tracked down by the Empire during the operation to secure the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] plans, she committed suicide by swallowing a lullaby<ref name="RD" />&mdash;[[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] slang for suicide pill<ref name="RAS">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>&mdash;knowing that she would more than likely be tortured if captured.<ref name="RD" /> According to Imperial documentation, another Rebel method was having an [[Affide crystal/Legends|affide crystal]] hidden under a waterproof barrier in a false tooth. The crystal could be pried loose with the tongue, releasing the poison.<ref name="RB" /> [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] was taught how to will herself to die, through what was said to be the most difficult mind-act there was, especially for someone young and healthy.<ref name="CTE" />

The infamous [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] had ways to ensure that those of his prisoners who were worth more alive than dead couldn't kill themselves before he could collect the bounty. If the person attempted to injure themselves, they would be restrained; if they tried to starve themselves, the victim would be brutally force-fed.<ref name="MA" />

===Death===
{{Quote|Died of complications from acute cardiopulmonary viral trauma.|Imperial euphemism for death during interrogation|<ref name="TTBSB" />}}
[[File:Shmidyng.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Shmi Skywalker dies in her son's arms]]
Shortly before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]], mother of Anakin Skywalker, was captured by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] and tortured for weeks.<ref name="CP" /> She died in the arms of her son, moments before he was able to successfully rescue her.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref>

During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], death during interrogation was not entirely uncommon. One example was [[Von Longo]], a prisoner on the [[Imperial prison barge]] [[Purge (prison barge)|''Purge'']], who died during interrogation at the hands of [[Captain of the Guard/Legends|Captain of the Guard]] [[Jareth Sartoris]].<ref name="DT" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Rebellion]], several [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] were tortured to death, including [[Shanda Dok]],<ref name="AIR" /> [[Tev Matthews]]<ref name="TTBSB" /> and [[Ten Numb/Legends|Ten Numb]].<ref name="XWRL" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], several Jedi suffered the same fate, like [[Swilja Fenn]]<ref name="EVI" /> and [[Yabeley]].<ref name="Emissary of the Void">"[[Emissary of the Void]]"</ref>

In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Ailyn Vel]] was led to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where she hid in a [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] community and was caught during the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]]'s raids. Believing her to be a [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] terrorist, Jacen Solo interrogated her. When she did not provide information, he used the Force to repeatedly slam her head into the table where she was sitting while attempting to enter her mind. The punishment was far more than Ailyn could endure, and she died while being questioned.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

Sometimes, another person would end the hapless torture victim's life,<ref name="NP" /><ref name="Harm">{{JournalCite|10|Do No Harm}}</ref> or kill a torture victim to be, as an act of compassion and mercy<ref name="SOTME" /> and/or to silence them before they could spill any secrets. During the Rebellion, the Rebel and [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] [[Aurin Leith]] was part of a team ordered to keep [[Gebnerret Vibrion]], the head of a Rebel cell imprisoned by the Galactic Empire on [[Selnesh/Legends|Selnesh]], from spilling any secrets, either by freeing him or killing him. Aurin was unhappy with the prospect of killing Vibrion, since it conflicted with her medical oath to "do no harm," but eventually agreed to give Vibrion a dose of [[conergin]] to knock him out if it became necessary for the others to kill him. Luckily, the team managed to rescue Vibrion.<ref name="Harm" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Hallena Devis]] worked as an agent for [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]], but eventually decided to quit her job; a key factor for her decision was having had to make sure torture victims got killed.<ref name="NP" />

==Behind the scenes==
Torture has been a part of ''Star Wars'' from the very beginning. In the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] tortures [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] with powerful electroshocks. In the incarnation of the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft of ''A New Hope'']], Leia is replaced by Deak Starkiller, brother of Luke Starkiller, who would become [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in later drafts. When the heroes find him inside his cell, there's a strange yellow glow in his eyes. In the third draft, Vader steps into Leia's cell, the door slams shut and "her screams can barely be heard." The [[IT-O interrogation droid/Legends|IT-O]] torture droid didn't appear until the fourth draft.<ref name="Anno">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>

In the movie, the door to Leia's cell slams shut before the viewer gets see what actually happens to Leia. In the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]], the interrogation session was vividly depicted in a psychologically intense scene which was so chilling that it prompted some complaints from a concerned listener.<ref name="Star Wars Insider 79">''Ask the Master'' in [[Star Wars Insider 79|''Star Wars Insider'' 79]]</ref>

For [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], director [[Irvin Kershner]] originally filmed more shots of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] being tortured,<ref name="Anno" /> which showed the machine in operation with spikes and needles and electronic things going,<ref name="EVDVD">DVD commentary for {{Film|V}}</ref> and flashes of electricity everywhere. It was cut because the filmmakers were afraid that this would be too intense for children. Some of Han's screaming off-screen was also taken out<ref name="Anno" /> for the same reason. According to the director, everyone felt that the cut material was too much for a film of this type.<ref name="EVDVD" />

In ''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]'', chapter fourteen, [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] describes a phenomenon in which hostages "sometimes grew strangely attached to their captors. Sometimes captives even grew to love their warders, particularly if the warder was skilled enough in manipulating people." This is known as the [[Wikipedia:Stockholm syndrome|Stockholm syndrome]].
